# FrameChord

> FrameChord is a local command-line tool, one binary, that turns YAML and Markdown briefs into images, infographics, speech, podcasts, audiobooks, music and sound effects through OpenAI, Google Gemini, Fish Audio, OpenRouter and ElevenLabs. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot drive it through a bundled skill. This file describes FrameChord 0.7.0.

Before you act for a user:

- Install: `curl -fsSL https://framechord.com/install.sh | sh` on macOS or Linux, `irm https://framechord.com/install.ps1 | iex` in Windows PowerShell. Check with `framechord --version`.
- Set up a project with `framechord init` at its root. It is offline, preserves existing files and installs the skill in `.claude/skills/framechord/` and `.agents/skills/framechord/`. Read that `SKILL.md` and its references before authoring files.
- Credentials come from the environment or the project `.env`: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `FISH_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`. Never print, paste or commit key values.
- Loop: author a YAML job and Markdown brief, run `framechord validate`, preview with `--dry-run --json` (no provider calls), show the user that preview and wait for their explicit approval before generating, then report the artifact paths from the JSON result. A request to make media is not approval of the preview.
- Pass `--json --non-interactive`. Keep scripts, lyrics and figures exact. Do not switch provider, model or voice unless asked. Get fresh approval before resuming a stopped run or batch, and never retry an uncertain paid request without explicit approval.
- A request for an audiobook, or to read a book or long document aloud, is `media: audiobook`: one narrator, the exact source text, one file per chapter and optionally the full book. A podcast is a multi-speaker conversation; do not turn a book into one unless the user asks.

## Guide

- [Full guide in Markdown](https://framechord.com/index.md): every section below and all 66 command pages
- [See & hear it](https://framechord.com/index.md#showcase): See and hear it — A six-slide narrated tour, a one-minute podcast and an original music bed. Every image, voice and note in this section was generated by FrameChord from the job files linked below. Nothing here was edited by hand except for compression for the web.
- [Hand it to your agent](https://framechord.com/index.md#delegate): You do not need to learn every flag. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot or any agent that can run commands can drive FrameChord for you. Say what you want in plain words; the agent writes the brief files, previews the request for free and asks before anything is billed.
- [Scenarios & use cases](https://framechord.com/index.md#scenarios): What do you want to make? — Nine practical scenarios, from a single narrated article to a package of images and audio. Choose a task to see its inputs, deliverables, exact commands and review steps.
- [Getting started](https://framechord.com/index.md#start): Set up once. Finish at your pace. — A guided terminal checklist with arrow-key choices, search and clear readiness. Initialization stays offline.
- [Pay per asset](https://framechord.com/index.md#cost): Pay per asset, not per month — FrameChord has no subscription, credits or account. Each request is billed by the provider you configured at its API list price; keys, inputs and receipts stay in your repository.
- [Use it in your project](https://framechord.com/index.md#integrate): Use it in your own project — Initialize inside an existing repository, commit the authored files, and call the binary from any script or agent.
- [Command basics](https://framechord.com/index.md#basics): One pattern, every medium — Tell the CLI what to create, what to read, which model to use, and where the result belongs.
- [Images](https://framechord.com/index.md#images): An image for an article — Create a cover, illustration or standalone visual from a specific creative brief.
- [Infographics](https://framechord.com/index.md#infographics): Make the facts part of the input — An infographic needs an exact content specification as well as visual direction. Keep copy and numeric strings in YAML.
- [Speech & narration](https://framechord.com/index.md#speech): Read an article aloud — Give the CLI the exact words to speak and a separate brief for delivery.
- [Podcasts](https://framechord.com/index.md#podcasts): Give each speaker a turn — Author the conversation explicitly. Each turn has its own script, model and voice; the CLI generates clips and assembles the episode.
- [Audiobooks](https://framechord.com/index.md#audiobooks): Read a whole book aloud — One narrator reads your exact text, chapter by chapter. Get a file per chapter, or the whole book with chapter markers, from a Markdown manuscript or an explicit chapter list.
- [Instrumental & vocal music](https://framechord.com/index.md#music): A music bed or an original song — Describe mood, instrumentation, structure and duration. Choose instrumental or vocal explicitly.
- [Sound effects](https://framechord.com/index.md#effects): Small sounds with a clear purpose — Specify the event, texture, duration and what should be absent.
- [Reusable characters](https://framechord.com/index.md#characters): Define identity once. Review every reuse. — Save stable visual and voice profiles separately from scene direction. Characters are optional for ordinary generation.
- [Saved & designed voices](https://framechord.com/index.md#voices): Reuse a saved voice, or design a candidate — Speech voice identity is independent of visual identity. Start with an accessible provider voice binding.
- [Agent integration & planning](https://framechord.com/index.md#agents): Use it from any agent with process access — The skill teaches authoring and review. The executable handles credentials, provider requests and local records.
- [Parallel generation](https://framechord.com/index.md#parallel): Run independent work together — Keep each job in its own manifest. A batch schedules independent jobs concurrently and preserves successes if another job fails.
- [Review, revise & recover](https://framechord.com/index.md#review): A saved file is the start of review — Generation success means a result was saved and checked structurally. It does not prove accurate text, voice quality or character identity.
- [Full reference](https://framechord.com/index.md#reference): The full command reference travels with you — Use built-in help for exact options and schemas for file contracts.
- [Every command & flag](https://framechord.com/index.md#commands): Every command. Every flag. — Exact bundled help for all 66 command pages. Expand an entry to inspect its options.
